points: The angel of the Lord sat under the oak in Ophrah while Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites, and said, the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: An angel of the Lord came and sat under an oak in Ophrah, while Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites; that is how hard the oppression sat on the land, that a man hid his own harvest to keep it.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Gideon answered, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us, and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? The Lord hath forsaken us and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites. Read chapters 6 through 8 for the rest of him.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: Gideon answers, oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us, and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us?
Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: When Gideon perceived he had seen an angel of the Lord face to face, he feared death, but the Lord said, peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die. Gideon built an altar there and called it Jehovah-shalom, which is, the Lord is peace.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the Lord said, but by night, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city; they worshipped that idol and would have killed him in the daylight.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: Now you know where the famous story of the three hundred came from: they got it from our ancestors, from Gideon. The nations take our history and make it entertainment, and even the artwork drew those three hundred with locks and braids and gave the other host the same, because the artist knew whose history he was drawing; those three hundred were Israelites.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The Lord put that dream into the mind of the enemy and sent Gideon down to hear it, so he could go into the battle valiant and strong, without any doubt. When Gideon heard the dream and the interpretation, he worshipped, and returned to say, arise; for the Lord hath delivered into your hand the host of Midian.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: Gideon and his hundred come to the outside of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but newly set the watch; in war you always have watchmen taking first, second, and third watch, and Gideon struck right in between the changing of the watchmen.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The three companies blew the trumpets, brake the pitchers, held the lamps in their left hands and the trumpets in their right, and cried, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon; and every man stood in his place round about the camp. Three hundred against thousands, you have to do something to mess with their mind: those horns blowing in unison put fear in the nations, and all the host ran, and cried, and fled.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The men of Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh gathered themselves and pursued after the Midianites, and Gideon sent messengers throughout all mount Ephraim to come down and take the waters before them; and Ephraim took two princes of Midian, slaying Oreb upon the rock Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: Gideon promises Succoth that when the Lord has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into his hand, he will tear their flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers; and when the men of Penuel answer him the same way, he promises to break down their tower when he comes again in peace.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents and smote the host while it was secure, and when the two kings fled, he pursued and took them, and discomfited all the host.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Zebah and Zalmunna say, rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. They wanted to die quick at the hand of a warrior rather than suffer under the sword of a boy; so Gideon arose and slew them, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels' necks.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: The men of Israel ask Gideon to rule over them, both he, his son, and his son's son, for delivering them from the hand of Midian. Israel has always needed a leader, because we are lost sheep; we need somebody to guide us in the way we must go, or we wander off the path of righteousness. It has always been that way, and you see it playing out right here.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon refuses: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you; the Lord shall rule over you.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon made an ephod thereof and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it, which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more, and the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon. Gideon had threescore and ten sons, for he had many wives, and his concubine in Shechem bare him a son whose name he called Abimelech; and Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: The sum of the history of Gideon, who is also named Jerubbaal, is this: the victory does not come in the strength of numbers, in how many guns or how many bullets you have. The victory of battle comes from the Lord, and that is why we have to trust in the Lord with all our heart and endure to the end, keeping these commandments until the return of our King of kings.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: It came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god, and remembered not the Lord their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side; neither shewed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Abimelech went to his mother's brethren in Shechem and put it to them: whether is better, that all the sons of Jerubbaal, threescore and ten persons, reign over you, or that one reign over you? Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.

note.label: Blood Toucheth Blood

points: Abimelech was the son of Jerubbaal by his concubine in Shechem. He went to Shechem unto his mother's brethren, his uncles on his mother's side, and had them ask the men of Shechem whether it was better for all seventy sons of Jerubbaal to reign over them, or for one man to reign.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: He went unto his father's house at Ophrah and slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, threescore and ten persons, upon one stone. He killed his own family to clear his way to a throne.
Notwithstanding, Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left, for he hid himself.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Jotham applied the parable: if ye have done truly and sincerely in that ye have made Abimelech king, and if ye have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: The cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal was laid upon Abimelech their brother, and upon the men of Shechem which aided him in the killing of his brethren. Guilty by association and by action: the blood cried, and the Lord put it back on them.

note.label: Blood Toucheth Blood

points: The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Gaal talked big: who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: for why should we serve him? He asked why they should be serving this Israelite at all.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal. Our forefather Jotham, a young man at the time, prophesied their destruction, and it came to pass.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

cases.charge: Throwing down his father’s altar of Baal; going against Midian with three hundred, as the Lord said
cases.preview: Israel hid in dens and caves in the mountains of their own land while Midian, Amalek and the eastern peoples swarmed in like locusts and destroyed the crops.

cases.name: Gideon’s ephod
cases.charge: Making an ephod of the golden earrings of the spoil, and putting it in Ophrah; all Israel going a whoring after it
cases.preview: The men of Israel asked Gideon to rule over them, and his son and grandson after him, for saving them from Midian, and he refused: the Lord would rule over them.

cases.name: Abimelech son of Gideon
cases.charge: Slaying his seventy brethren upon one stone with silver out of the house of Baal-berith; making himself king at Shechem
cases.preview: Gideon’s son by his concubine in Shechem went to his mother’s kin and told them to remember he was their own flesh and blood, and they chose him by kinship rather than by righteousness.
